description: Measures an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with EvalScope 1.14.1, pinned by version and by a hash-locked requirements file, in two parts. Throughput, the main result, runs `evalscope perf` on fixed workloads: prefill at 2k, 8k, 32k, and 128k prompt tokens with one output token; decode of 256 output tokens at 128, 8k, and 32k tokens of context; closed-loop concurrency of 1, 2, 4, and 8 with 512 input and 64 output tokens; and a five-turn conversation of 8k tokens per turn that exercises the prefix cache. Prompts are EvalScope's random token prompts, reseeded for every level and pass, so no prompt repeats; length is forced with ignore_eos, and a level whose requests fail, miss the target input length, or do not produce exactly the target output length is excluded and its pass is failed. Prefill is processed input tokens over EvalScope's time to first token. Decode is output tokens minus one over its time per output token. Output throughput is output tokens over the test duration. All are ratios of sums. Warm-up requests inside each level and optional warm-up passes are excluded; formal pass counts come from the experiment contract (--warmup, --repetitions). Intelligence runs `evalscope eval` on rule-scored benchmarks only, with no judge model: HumanEval (all 164 tasks, pass@1, official tests executed in a Docker sandbox with no network, a digest-pinned image, 1 GiB, and 1 CPU) and GSM8K (4-shot, the first 200 test questions, final-number match), at temperature 0 with a 4096-token output limit. It exists to show that the engine still computes the model correctly: the scores are reported with their standard errors and judged against a baseline engine of the same model by the experiment, not by an absolute floor. Datasets are the pinned ModelScope files, checked by SHA-256 and copied before use. Before every run the driver repeats its negative control through the same EvalScope pipeline: a reference engine with known prefill and decode rates, two decode slots, and a prefix cache, whose rates, concurrency scaling, and prefix reuse must be recovered; injected faults (early stops, HTTP errors, a missing prefix cache) that must be caught; and an oracle engine that must score right answers 1, wrong answers 0, and show that generated code cannot reach the network from the sandbox (a probe must run cleanly with the network disabled and fail with it enabled). Cold load is not measured. Peak memory is sampled only with --memory-pid, and swap-out is the whole-machine delta on a loopback endpoint.
cache_policy: No prefix reuse across requests: EvalScope's random prompts are reseeded for every level and pass, so no prompt repeats and reported cached tokens are expected to be zero (more than 1% fails the level). The turns of a multi-turn conversation reuse their own earlier turns, and the reported cache hit ratio is recorded without being required. Engines that report no cached tokens are recorded as unverified.
